Topic: The Transformational View of Derivatives: From Motion to Mapping

Target audience: University students (Calculus I beginners)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite: The Concept of a 'Function as a Map'

Lecture lines:
Functions transform inputs into outputs.
Imagine a rubber band stretching.
Points map to new positions.
The derivative measures local density.
Transformations change spatial relationships.

Planned animations:
Display a set A on the left and set B on the right. (#FFFFFF)
Draw a dynamic arrow f(x) from an element x in A to f(x) in B. (#3498DB)
Show multiple parallel arrows illustrating the mapping process for different elements. (#F1C40F)

Section: section_2 — The Derivative as a Local Scaling Factor

Lecture lines:
Derivatives act as local scaling factors.
Think of a cheetah running.
Velocity maps time to distance.

Planned animations:
Draw a curve representing a function f. (#FFFFFF)
Place a zoom-in circle around a point x. (#E74C3C)
Show the local tangent line segment approximating the curve slope. (#2ECC71)

Section: section_3 — Visualizing the Linear Approximation (Tangent as a Linear Map)

Lecture lines:
Tangent lines approximate curves linearly.
Zoom in to see straight lines.
Curves become simple linear maps.
The slope is the scale.
Linearity simplifies complex motion.

Planned animations:
Visualize the function as a rubber sheet. (#FFFFFF)
Apply a grid transformation to show linear local behavior. (#3498DB)
Highlight the tangent plane as the best flat approximation. (#E74C3C)

Section: section_4 — Application: The Jacobian and Multivariable Intuition

Lecture lines:
Jacobians extend transformations to 2D.
Squares map to parallelograms.
Robot arms trace paths beautifully.

Planned animations:
Show a 2D to 2D vector field transformation. (#FFFFFF)
Represent the Jacobian matrix as a set of basis vectors. (#F1C40F)
Demonstrate the local stretching and rotation of a small patch. (#2ECC71)

Section: section_5 — Summary: Derivative as the 'Local Geometry Modifier'

Lecture lines:
Derivative is a local modifier.
It warps the input space.
Compare constant, linear, quadratic stretches.

Planned animations:
Display the core idea: Derivative = Local Geometry Modifier. (#FFFFFF)
Animate the zoom-in from global curve to local tangent. (#3498DB)
Show the transition from space to flat approximation. (#E74C3C)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
